roles.name: Switcher & Livestream
roles.short: Cut the service and get it online. One person, one desk.
roles.overview: The Switcher & Livestream operator runs the ATEM switcher and the YouTube livestream from one desk. During the week you check who is on cameras. On Sunday you arrive by 9:00 to set up and rehearse, go live at 10:15, call the shots to the camera team on headsets and cut the service, then save everything, update YouTube and shut down. A win is a stream confirmed live in YouTube Studio before the service, cuts that follow the worship and the preacher, and a recording saved in vMix every week.

prep.title: Check who is on cameras
steps: Open the Services app in Planning Center and check who is rostered on cameras this Sunday.
Check in with the team during the week so everyone knows they're on.

steps.t: Arrive by 9:00.
Make sure the console power is on.
sub: The Sound operator switches on the power for the whole console.
The ATEM Television Studio HD8 comes on with the console power.

steps.t: Turn on the computer.
Turn on the cameras.
Open ATEM Software Control (Blackmagic) and vMix.
In ATEM Software Control, go to File > Restore.
Select the setup file. It is the only file in the folder.
sub: File name: to be confirmed.
steps.note: The setup file holds the input mapping, so nothing needs remapping.

pre.title: Check every camera is live

steps.t: The buttons on the HD8 are labelled. You switch using these buttons.
sub: Front: main central camera
Back: left back angle, about 20 degrees
Roaming: the handheld camera
Drum cam: fixed
Keys cam: fixed

steps: On the ATEM multiview monitor, check every camera is showing a picture.

steps.t: In the vMix multiview, check the ATEM feed and the ProPresenter feed are both showing.
sub: The ATEM comes into vMix over HDMI.
ProPresenter lyrics and overlays come into vMix over NDI with a transparent background, so they sit over the ATEM picture.

steps.t: If a camera is black, check its power and cables, then the cables at the ATEM. For Roaming, check the battery.
steps.note: See the troubleshooting guide: Camera is black on the multiview.

pre.title: Baptism Sundays: set up the tank camera
steps: An extra NDI camera is mounted, focused on the baptism tank.
The camera team and the Switcher set it up together.
It comes into the ATEM through an NDI to SDI converter, so it is on the HD8 like the other cameras.
ProPresenter can also take it directly for the room screens.

pre.title: Rehearse
steps: Rehearsal runs from 9:00 to 9:45.
Rehearse camera shots and timing with the camera operators.
Use the time for testing.

pre.title: Pre-service check-ins
steps: Camera operators: in place and ready to roll.

steps.t: Headsets: check every camera operator can hear you.
sub: You call the cues during the service.

steps.t: Sound: check the stream audio is coming through. Listen on headphones.
sub: Stream audio comes straight from the sound desk over Dante.
The Sound operator checks the levels. You listen on headphones as well.

steps.t: ProPresenter: check all the overlays are coming through in vMix.
sub: The ProPresenter operator fires lyrics, lower thirds and overlays. The overlay channel in vMix stays on, so you don't need to do anything.

pre.title: Go live and confirm on YouTube

steps.t: ProPresenter sends the welcome loop.
In vMix, click Stream.
sub: We use the same stream key every week, so there's nothing to set up in YouTube first.
Stream settings are saved: 1080p, 30fps, 6500 kbps. Don't change them.

steps.t: On the same computer, open YouTube Studio and look for the live signal.
steps.note: This is the most important check of the day. Don't trust vMix alone. Confirm in YouTube Studio that the stream is live before the service starts.

steps.t: At 10:27 ProPresenter plays the countdown (ramp-up) video over the top.
Nothing to do while it plays. When ProPresenter clears it, your ATEM picture shows.
Have Front ready: medium close-up on the worship leader.
At 10:30, click Record in vMix.
steps.note: Record every week. This is the step people forget.

steps.t: Hold Front on the worship leader, medium close-up, for 5 to 10 seconds.
Then move across to a wide shot or an instrument shot.

live.title: Worship switching
steps: Cut every few seconds.
Cuts only. No fades or other transitions.
Feature instruments when they are soloing or prominent (Drum cam, Keys cam).
Use every camera, multiple times, with multiple shots from each. Call the shots to the camera operators on headsets.

live.title: Sermon switching
steps: Use Front and Back.
Each shot stays up for at least 10 seconds and no longer than 45 seconds.

steps.t: Use Roaming occasionally.
sub: Roaming shoots from the back, with a slight sideways move across the congregation's heads towards the preacher.

live.title: Videos and announcements
steps: ProPresenter plays bumper and announcement videos full screen over the top in vMix.

steps.t: You don't need to do anything.
steps.note: If you have turned off the overlay channel in vMix, the videos won't show. Select it again.

live.title: Baptisms and altar calls
steps: Baptisms: you have two options, the tank camera and Roaming.
Altar calls: try not to film people being prayed for.

steps.t: Extended altar call: end the livestream.
steps.note: This is the only time we stop the stream during the service.

live.title: Keep an eye on the stream
steps: Listen to the stream audio on headphones.
Watch vMix for any errors.
Check the stream health (stream quality) indicator in YouTube Studio.
To kill the ProPresenter graphics, deselect the overlay channel in vMix.

steps.t: After the blessing, click the closing slide in the vMix inputs so it goes to the livestream.
sub: How long the closing slide stays up: to be confirmed.

steps.t: Stop recording in vMix.
Stop streaming in vMix.

down.title: Update the YouTube title and description

steps.t: In YouTube Studio, open the live stream and choose edit title and description.
Add the sermon title and the speaker.
sub: Post-production is handled separately. YouTube takes about 12 to 24 hours before the stream is ready for it.

steps.t: Save the ATEM file before closing.
steps.note: Always save the ATEM file before you close ATEM Software Control.

steps.t: Close vMix and ATEM Software Control.
Turn off the cameras.
Shut down the computer.
Put the Roaming camera battery on charge.
The Sound operator turns off the console power, which also turns off the HD8.

fixes.title: Camera is black on the multiview
fixes.when: Use this when one of the cameras shows black on the ATEM or vMix multiview.
steps: Check the camera is powered on.
Check the cables at the camera.
Check the cables at the ATEM end.
If it's Roaming, check the camera battery.

fixes.title: Internet is down
fixes.when: Use this when the internet drops and the stream can't go out.
steps: There is no backup internet, so don't try to switch connections.
Make sure vMix is recording. If it isn't, click Record.
Carry on switching the service so the recording is complete.

rules: Don't load a new setup file mid-service.
Don't try an untested transition. We use cuts only.
Don't update ATEM, vMix or computer software on a Sunday.
Don't change the stream settings or bitrate mid-stream.
Don't stop streaming in vMix during the service, except for an extended altar call.
Don't assume the stream is live without checking YouTube Studio.
Don't film people being prayed for at altar calls.
handoff: The HD8 buttons are labelled, and the input mapping loads from the setup file.
Setup file: ATEM Software Control, File > Restore. It's the only file in the folder.
10:15: click Stream in vMix, then confirm it's live in YouTube Studio. 10:30: click Record.
No logins needed. YouTube Studio and vMix are already set up on the computer.
No backup internet. If it drops, keep recording in vMix.
The camera roster is in the Planning Center Services app.
Anything else: call the Team Leader.

roles.name: Sound
roles.short: Mix the room and the stream so every word is heard.
roles.overview: The sound operator makes sure everyone in the room and online can clearly hear every word spoken and sung. You arrive before rehearsal to power up and line check, mix the band and speakers through the service, and shut the system down safely afterwards. A win on Sunday is a service where nobody notices the sound because it simply works.

steps.t: Switch on main power for the desk and stage boxes.
Turn on the mixing desk and the playback computer.
sub: Wait for the desk to fully load its show file before touching faders.

steps.t: Turn on amps and powered speakers last.
steps.note: Speakers go on last and off first, so they never pop.

pre.title: Check batteries and wireless mics
steps: Put charged batteries in every handheld and headset mic.
Confirm each receiver shows signal and battery level.

steps.t: Swap any battery showing two bars or less.
steps.note: Low batteries rarely die in rehearsal. They die in the sermon.

steps.t: Ask each musician and vocalist to play or speak one at a time.
Confirm the signal lands on the correct channel and the label matches.
Note anything missing and fix it before rehearsal starts.
Have the person sing or play at their loudest normal level.
Raise the gain until the meter sits healthily without reaching the red.
steps.note: Set gain at rehearsal volume, not soundcheck politeness. People always get louder.

pre.title: Rehearsal mix and monitors
steps: Build a rough front-of-house mix while the band runs the set.
Check every musician is happy with what they hear before rehearsal ends.
Save the scene once rehearsal is done.

live.title: Before the countdown
steps: Walk-in music playing at a comfortable level.
Host and pastor mics on, checked and muted until needed.
Band channels ready for the opening song.

live.title: Quick mixing reminders
steps: Vocals sit on top of the band. Words matter most.
Watch the stage, not just the desk. Unmute before someone speaks, not after.

steps.t: Keep an eye on the stream mix as well as the room.
steps.note: The room is loud. The stream only hears the desk.

steps.t: Worship to host: bring up the host mic as the last song ends.
Host to sermon: bring up the pastor's mic and pull down band channels.
Sermon to response: bring the band back in gently as they start.
Turn off amps and powered speakers first.
Shut down the playback computer and the desk.
Switch off main power last.
steps.note: This is the start-up order in reverse.

down.title: Pack away mics and batteries
steps: Return every wireless mic to its home.
Put used batteries on charge.
Coil cables over-under and put them away.

down.title: Report anything that went wrong
steps: Tell your team leader about any issue before you leave.
If you fixed something new, record a quick phone video of how, so it can become a troubleshooting guide.

fixes.title: Wireless mic has no sound
fixes.when: Use this when a wireless mic is switched on but nothing comes through the speakers.
steps: Check the mute switch on the mic itself.
Check the battery level on the mic and the receiver.
Make sure the receiver shows a signal.
Check the channel is unmuted and the fader is up on the desk.
Swap to the backup mic and sort the first one after the service.
stuck: Hand the speaker a wired mic.
